messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: GPU Xid/driver-reset wave detected in cluster infer-prod-us-east-1a. ~12 resets in last 3m affecting gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-22. Symptoms: containers killed (SIGKILL), CUDA Xid 43/31 observed, intermittent high ECC correctable counts. Runbook: /runbooks/gpu-driver-reset. @sre-jen you're oncall for this page.

sre-jen: ack — joining. Starting triage: collecting node/journal and pod logs. Can someone paste `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep infer` for the affected nodes?

kai: I pulled node logs — nv-hostengine shows repeated resets, and dmesg has `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:AF:00): 43` spam. ECC correctable errors spiked before the first reset. My recommendation: cordon gpu-node-17 and drain non-critical pods ASAP to stop rippling.

mara: customer-impact notes: two enterprise tenants reporting increased 500s and timeouts around the same timestamps. Telemetry correlates request timeouts with container restarts. CS notified; will open bridge if this persists. :alert: 

devon: propose immediate traffic fallback to a lighter/quantized model for the affected routes to reduce memory pressure and keep SLAs. We can flip routing to redwood-model-v1-quant in the router for /generate for 100% until nodes stabilise.

kai: commands to run for mitigation/diagnostics:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
ssh ops@gpu-node-17 'sudo journalctl -u nv-hostengine -n 200 | tail -n 80'
# on node:
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,retired_pages --format=csv
edac-util --report
```

sre-jen: executing drain now. Observed container runtime log excerpt showing OOM before driver reset: 
```
E tensorflow/core/common_runtime/gpu/gpu_device.cc: failed to allocate 104857600 bytes: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
... runtime: killed by signal 9
```
This suggests processes were hitting device memory limits right before the Xid.

ops-bot: node gpu-node-17 cordoned by @kai and drain started — 12 pods will be evicted. Migration webhook triggered. :white_check_mark:

mara: CS update sent to affected customers A and B; status page updated to "investigating". Account teams looped in.

devon: router fallback applied to reduce load on GPUs: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://router.internal/api/routes/fallback -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"route":"/generate","fallback_model":"redwood-model-v1-quant","percent":100}'
```
Confirmed majority of inbound inference now routed to quant variant. Monitoring for quality/regression.

sre-jen: kernel/dmesg shows Xid 43 pattern repeating — driver reset at 16:48:12 UTC and again at 16:50:07 UTC. If resets persist after drain, I'll schedule a node reboot and escalate to hardware diagnostics (possible ECC/rack-level issues).

kai: telemetry snapshot: ECC correctable errors jumped from ~4/min -> ~60/min in the 5m window preceding the first reset. Please capture `edac-util` output and `sudo smartctl -a` for the node.

oncall-b: I'll be taking handoff in ~8m. Please post a concise TL;DR and outstanding actions I should monitor.

sre-jen: handoff summary for @oncall-b: 
- Root cause (suspected): ECC correctable spike causing GPU driver instability -> Xid 43 resets -> containers killed / OOM patterns.
- Actions taken: cordoned + drained gpu-node-17 (in progress), enabled router fallback to redwood-model-v1-quant, notified CS and status page, collecting kernel/journal/container logs and `edac-util` output.
- Next steps for oncall-b: watch for further Xid spikes, confirm drained node remains stable, if resets continue reboot node and isolate from pool; create hardware ticket with diagnostics (attach nv-hostengine dump and dmesg).

mara: I added an incident checklist in this channel with ticket refs, customers, and mitigation timeline. Also flagged finance/customer success for billing/credits analysis if SLA hit.

sre-jen: posting key snippets for postmortem: 
```
# dmesg excerpt
[37542.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:AF:00): 43, PID=2145, GPU=0, File:..
# nv-hostengine tail
[INFO] Resetting GPU driver due to watchdog failure
```
Please grab `sudo nv-hostengine --dump` and the full `journalctl -u nv-hostengine` output before reboot.

ops-bot: drain complete on gpu-node-17, pods migrated to pool-infer-fallback. Node is now unschedulable.

sre-jen: preparing to reboot gpu-node-17 for clean driver bring-up after captures are uploaded to /artifacts/incidents/5512349876/. I'll wait 2m for oncall-b before performing; otherwise proceed with reboot.

oncall-b: taking the incident. Thanks @sre-jen — I'll own monitoring and customer comms. Please leave any unfinished diagnostics in the incident artifact dir. Escalate to hardware if Xids persist after reboot.

mara: closing loop: CS will keep customers updated every 30m; incident severity set to P1, next update in ~20m unless resolved earlier. :memo:

sre-jen: final note before handing off: capture `nvidia-smi -q` and `sudo edac-util --report` and include them in the hardware ticket. Moving to quiet period; handing to @oncall-b.

(reacted :thumbsup: by kai, :eyes: by devon)
